episode_summary: Dee, Corey Petty and Jesse Broke give a technical explainer on the Bitcoin upgrade merged into Bitcoin Core in October 2020: Schnorr signatures (BIP 340), Taproot (BIP 341) and Tapscript. They cover signature aggregation, MAST, the Schnorr patent history and why the code being merged did not mean the upgrade was active. The roundtable then covers BrightID, the Circles UBI project and the Honey token.

cards.claim: In October 2020 a host predicted that if Taproot activated within a year, it would bring a tremendous boom of development on top of the Bitcoin blockchain.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: if this gets through if this gets through within a year you're going to see a tremendous boom of development on top of the bitcoin blockchain

cards.claim: In October 2020 the hosts said the Taproot and Schnorr code had been merged into Bitcoin Core but was not yet usable on the Bitcoin network.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: It's just in the code base, meaning that you still can't create transactions that use these technologies and they be valid on the network.

cards.claim: In October 2020 a host said Taproot might take over a year to activate because the community had not yet settled on an activation process.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: It may be over a year until the community decides, okay, this is the activation process.

cards.claim: In October 2020 a host explained that Schnorr signatures replace the many signatures in a multi-input spend with a single signature.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: instead of including all of those signatures, I include one signature.

cards.claim: In October 2020 a host gave a one-sentence definition of Taproot as the aggregation of addresses for merkelized abstract syntax trees.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: the aggregation of addresses for merkelized abstract syntax trees

cards.claim: In October 2020 a host explained that MAST lets a spender reveal only the script branch actually used, keeping the other possible spending conditions private.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: when I publish, I'm only publishing the option that I chose and was proven true

cards.claim: In October 2020 a host said MAST transactions were impractically large before Schnorr signatures because every option's signatures had to be published together.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: But the downfall of MAST before Schnorr signatures is that you're going to publish all of those signatures at the same time

cards.claim: In October 2020 a host explained the UTXO model: sending money means gathering enough unspent outputs, each tied to a different key.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: If I want to send money to one of you, I have to look into all the UTXOs

cards.claim: In October 2020 a host said Schnorr-based transactions would largely remove chain analysts' ability to deduce what a transaction does, because all transactions look the same.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: all of my ability to deduce what's happening at a transactional level is gone

cards.claim: In October 2020 a host stated that Tapscript is the set of changes to Bitcoin's script language that let nodes verify Schnorr signatures and Taproot.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: TapScript is basically the necessary changes to the script language in Bitcoin to allow nodes to be able to verify whether or not these things are true

cards.claim: In October 2020 a host said the Schnorr patent officially expired in 2008, but the algorithm was not yet widely available in open source libraries.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: I think that officially the patent expired in 2008 but it hadn't been um around enough and and available to people

cards.claim: In October 2020 a host argued that Satoshi chose ECDSA over Schnorr because the Schnorr patent kept it out of the open source libraries available when he wrote the first client.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: he chose ecdsa and that's the reason why we have ecdsa signatures prolific across all of blockchain

cards.claim: In October 2020 a host said Bitcoin Cash had novel technology while being openly hostile to Roger Ver.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: Bitcoin Cash has novel technology and implementations.

cards.claim: In October 2020 a host predicted that Circles would never become something people spend, saying it was never going to be a thing.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: No, that's fucking never going to be a thing.

cards.claim: In October 2020 a host said Circles gave new members a 100% initial payout and described a claimed 700% inflation rate.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: You get 100% initially for an initial payout

cards.claim: In October 2020 the hosts said one Honey token was worth $1,111.16 according to the onehive.org site.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: one honey is 1111.16 for one honey token

cards.claim: In October 2020 a host said the price of Bitcoin was about $11,500 and the price of Ether about $350.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: the price of Bitcoin right now is about 11,500

cards.claim: In October 2020 a host explained that BrightID is a social-graph method for proving a user is a human, without requiring personal identifying information.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: BrightID is a method for an anti-spam mechanism, right? It's a way for you to prove you're a human

cards.claim: In October 2020 a host said the initiator of the Circles project was Martin Koppelman.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: So the initiator, according to the team, is Martin Koppelman.

cards.claim: In October 2020 a host called the Circles project a cash grab run by six people who would make a lot of money.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: it's just a cash grab it's just those six people on that website are going to make a lot of money

cards.claim: In October 2020 the hosts debated whether experimental crypto projects are worth attention, with one saying almost all of them would become nothing.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: almost all of them will become nothing like you

cards.claim: In October 2020 a host explained the halo theory with DeFi: to use DeFi you first had to hold Ether.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: in order to use DeFi you got to have Ether so that's some exclusivity right there

cards.claim: In October 2020 a host predicted that the halo moment for crypto would come from Wall Street, the same people Bitcoin had promised to phase out middlemen against.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: it's actually going to come from the same people that bitcoin uh gained popularity that also bitcoin promised to phase out the middlemen

cards.claim: In October 2020 a host explained the Halo theory using his own story: he bought an Xbox only after he needed it to play Halo with a friend.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: everyone who bought an xbox bought it because of halo

title: The Bitcoin Podcast #325- Hocus Pocus Bitcoin Upgrade
